text:
Maya (CSE): Hey team, AcmeCorp reported that when their Okta admin changed the mapping of the Okta group `engineering-contractors` from role `contractor` -> `infra_viewer`, users in that group didn't get their previous roles removed. Some users ended up with both roles. They say Okta's group push shows 200 for user adds but 403 on PATCH for removals.

Jasper (Eng-API): Can you paste the Okta log snippet and the SCIM request/response?

Maya (CSE): Paste below (redacted token). Note timestamp ~ 2026-01-12 from the customer's Okta admin: 
```
PATCH https://api.redwood.company/scim/v2/Users/00u1abcd1234
Authorization: Bearer scim_integration_key_redacted
Body: { "Operations": [ { "op": "remove", "path": "groups[display eq \"engineering-contractors\"]" } ] }

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "insufficient_scope", "error_description": "token missing scope: scim.groups:write" }
```

Maya (CSE): They also sent a 200 on group add events (POST /Groups) but the deletes are PATCHes and failing.

Ruth (IAM): Looks like their Okta SCIM app is using a token we issued earlier that only had user write scopes but not group write. We recently split scopes to be explicit: `scim.users:write` and `scim.groups:write`. If the token was minted before the change and got rotated to a scoped token, removals that rely on `scim.groups:write` will 403.

Lina (SRE): Quick question — are we rejecting PATCH semantics in any case for group membership removal? We allow both PATCH and PUT, but we enforce scopes per resource.

Jasper (Eng-API): Confirming — authorization layer checks resource+verb. The log error is our standard message for scope mismatch. We also have a nuance: when Okta does group push, it sometimes sends `Operations` targeting `members` vs `groups[...]` depending on their app template. Both flows rely on `scim.groups:write` for group membership deltas.

Maya (CSE): Customer says they rotated the token recently and didn't realize the new token lacked group scopes. Their Okta admin says Okta UI shows one token field and they pasted it into the app.

Ruth (IAM): Root cause: token scope mismatch. Secondary issue: because our existing role mapping job is eventually consistent, if deletions fail, the role-removal reconciliation job didn't immediately remove the orphaned role binding. That left users with both roles until reconciliation ran.

Lina (SRE): Repro steps I used on staging:
1) Create scoped token with `scim.users:write` only
2) Create group and add user via POST /Groups -> 200
3) Attempt to remove user via PATCH /Users/:id with group remove -> 403 (insufficient_scope)

Command I ran:
```bash
curl -X PATCH \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"groups[display eq \"eng-contractors\"]"}]}' \ 
  https://staging.api.redwood.company/scim/v2/Users/00u-staging-123
# => 403 + {"error":"insufficient_scope"}
```

Jasper (Eng-API): Possible mitigations:
- Short term: Customer must rotate/create a token with both `scim.users:write` and `scim.groups:write` and update the Okta app config. We can provide a prefilled token creation UI snippet.
- Medium term: Add clearer error text + guidance in the response with a reference link to our SCIM token scope docs so admins can self-fix.
- Longer term: Allow an admin-level token alias that retains backwards-compat before we enforce split scopes (but that's a policy decision).

Maya (CSE): Customer asked for a one-click way — they want instructions to test and force a reconciliation now.

Lina (SRE): We can trigger a manual reconciliation for their org. Steps we used for the customer:
1) Customer provides org-id and a maintenance window (we recommend 1-2 min).
2) We run our admin reconcile endpoint: `POST /admin/provisioning/reconcile?org=acme` (requires ops token).
3) If reconciliation can't remove stale roles due to continued 403s, we pause Okta pushes and reconcile offline.

Ruth (IAM): Also added a safety checklist for CSEs: verify token scopes before advising re-sync. Quick curl to inspect token scopes (returns list of scopes we issued):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer scim_integration_key_redacted" \ 
  https://api.redwood.company/admin/token-info
# => { "scopes": ["scim.users:write"] }
```

Maya (CSE): I sent the checklist and token-inspect curl to the Okta admin. They replied they see only `scim.users:write`. They created new token with both scopes and updated the app.

scim-sync-bot: triggered reconcile job for org=acme at 2026-01-12T15:23Z (job id: reconcile-20260112-acme-7)

Lina (SRE): Reconcile job output (sanitized):
```
- scanned 4,312 users
- fixed 18 orphaned role bindings by removing `contractor` role where group no longer matched mapping
- flagged 5 users for manual review (externalId collision)
- runtime 42s
```

Maya (CSE): Customer confirmed after reconcile that roles are now correct. They also asked for a doc page to avoid this in future.

Jasper (Eng-API): Action items:
- (Eng-API) add clearer scope error with link in 2 days (PR queued) — Jira INF-7721
- (IAM) add token-inspect endpoint to CSE playbook page — Ruth
- (SRE) add reconcile button to support console (ops-only) — Lina (design sync next week)

Ruth (IAM): I'll also add expirations and a recommended scope template for Okta SCIM app in docs.

Maya (CSE): Closing note for CSEs: when customers report partial deprovision with Okta pushes, first ask for token-inspect output and Okta debug logs (push history + example PATCH body). That triage step saved this case. :thumbsup:

Lina (SRE): Marking thread resolved — will follow up once PR and docs are live. :white_check_mark:
